n: Don’t envy wicked people or want to hang out with them.

f.w: Be not thou envious against evil men

n: Their hearts plot violence and their lips talk about causing trouble.
A household—a family and a life—is built by wisdom and made secure by understanding.

f.w: Through wisdom is an house builded

n: Knowledge fills its rooms with rare and beautiful treasures. A wise home is rich in more than possessions.
Wisdom is a kind of strength; knowledge increases power.
Wage war with careful strategy; many advisers bring victory.

f.w: in multitude of counsellors there is safety

n: Wisdom is out of a fool’s reach; he has nothing to say when serious matters are discussed at the city gate.

f.g: Where elders met to decide community matters.

n: Whoever plans evil will be known as a schemer.
Scheming folly is sin, and people detest a mocker.

f.w: The thought of foolishness is sin

n: If you give up when trouble comes, your strength is small. Hard times reveal real strength. (A play on words in Hebrew: “trouble” and “small” sound alike.)

f.w: If thou faint in the day of adversity

n: Rescue people being led away to death; don’t hold back from saving those stumbling toward slaughter.

f.w: deliver them that are drawn unto death

n: If you claim, “We didn’t know,” the God who weighs hearts knows better. He sees what we could have done and will repay everyone by their works.

f.w: render to every man according to his works

n: Eat honey, my child, because it is good and sweet.
Wisdom is sweet like honey to your soul. Find it, and your future is secure and your hope will not be disappointed.

f.w: thy expectation shall not be cut off

n: A warning to the wicked: don’t ambush the home of the righteous or raid their dwelling.
The righteous may fall many times, but they get back up; the wicked are brought down by disaster. Resilience, not perfection, marks the righteous—a comforting verse about repentance and perseverance.

f.w: a just man falleth seven times, and riseth up again

n: Don’t gloat when your enemy falls or rejoice when he stumbles.

f.w: Rejoice not when thine enemy falleth

n: The Lord might be displeased and turn his anger from your enemy—to you. Gloating is itself a sin.
Don’t fret over evildoers or envy the wicked.

f.w: Fret not thyself because of evil men

n: The evil have no future; their lamp will be snuffed out.

f.w: the candle of the wicked shall be put out

n: Revere the Lord and the king, and don’t join rebels.

f.w: fear thou the LORD and the king
them that are given to change
f.g: Those who are rebellious or revolutionary.

n: Disaster from both will come suddenly—who knows what ruin they can bring? This ends the “words of the wise” section.
A short appendix begins: more sayings of the wise. Showing favoritism in court is wrong.

f.w: These things also belong to the wise
f.g: A heading for an added collection (24:23–34).

n: A judge who tells the guilty “you’re innocent” will be cursed by people and hated by nations.
But those who convict the guilty will be blessed and things will go well for them.

f.g: Those who rightly convict the guilty.

n: An honest answer is like a kiss on the lips—a sign of true friendship.

f.g: A gesture of affection and loyalty.

n: Get your fields ready and your income secure, then build your house. Do first things first—sound advice for planning a life or a family.
Don’t testify against your neighbor without reason or use your words to deceive.

f.w: Be not a witness against thy neighbour without cause

n: Don’t say, “I’ll pay him back for what he did.” Revenge is forbidden; leave it to God.

f.w: I will do so to him as he hath done to me

n: A short story: the teacher passes the field and vineyard of a lazy man with no sense.
It is overgrown with thorns and weeds, and its stone wall has collapsed. Neglect slowly ruins what could be fruitful.
He looked closely, thought it over, and learned a lesson. Wisdom learns from observing life.
The lazy man’s motto: just a little more sleep. (Repeats 6:10.)

f.w: a little folding of the hands

n: Poverty comes like a robber and scarcity like an armed soldier. (Repeats 6:11.) Small habits of neglect lead to big losses.
